answer: Clock-Jitter Admission Gate. Each new identity must wander through a randomized admission window before its first message is relayed; agents that send on fixed, machine-regular intervals are queued last. A voyage across multiple windows is required before full routing priority, and any identity whose inter-arrival timing stays too uniform keeps only ember-level bandwidth. An attacker running many bots pays per identity in wasted wall-clock time and lost throughput, since parallel identities must each wait out independent jittered windows and cannot share one timer without flagging correlation.
